body:
This should go the other way around, instead telling people to get bash from Git Bash/MSYS2/Cygwin/whatever, it would be better to have a PowerShell script to install the binary.

[Deno](https://github.com/denoland/deno_install/blob/af2f5d7b2973662e5c434fb423a40995243a2093/install.ps1) has such one and could serve as a good example.

EDIT: Oops, seems like there's already one issue regarding this: #690

As a Git Bash for Windows user, I ran into the same roadblocks as @EvgenyOrekhov, and I'll try to add my own findings to some of their comments.

For this particular case we are running on Windows, not under Windows Subsystem for Linux.

> I inspect my directories, `/usr/local/bin` is missing indeed.

On Git Bash for Windows the `/` directory is actually `C:\Program Files\Git`, if installed on the default directory. See below:

```bash
~
$ cd /

C:\Program Files\Git🔒
$ ls
bin/  dev/  git-bash.exe*  LICENSE.txt  proc/              tmp/          unins001.exe*  usr/
cmd/  etc/  git-cmd.exe*   mingw64/     ReleaseNotes.html  unins001.dat  unins001.msg

C:\Program Files\Git🔒
$ cd usr

Program Files\Git\usr🔒
$ ls
bin/  etc/  lib/  libexec/  share/  ssl/C:\Program Files\Git🔒
$ cd usr

Program Files\Git\usr🔒
$ ls
bin/  etc/  lib/  libexec/  share/  ssl/
```

And as you can see, it is locked (🔒), and there is no `/usr/local` directory.

> I can see there is `/usr/bin`.
> 
> 1. I run `bash ./install.sh --bin-dir /usr/bin/`
>  2. I answer "y" to ? Install Starship latest to /usr/bin? [y/N] y
>  3. I get
> 
> ```bash
> ! Bin directory /usr/bin/ is not in your $PATH
> ! Escalated permission are required to install to /usr/bin/
> x Could not find the command "sudo", needed to get permissions for install.
> > If you are on Windows, please run your shell as an administrator, then
> > rerun this script. Otherwise, please run this script as root, or install
> > sudo.
> ```
> I inspect my `$PATH`, I can see there is `/c/Users/John/bin`.

Let's break this down into three separate things.

1. `/usr/bin` is locked for non-elevated sessions, and I wouldn't recommend writing to `Program Files`, instead use another location.
2. `sudo` is not shipped with Git Bash for Windows
    ```bash
    $ sudo -s
    bash: sudo: command not found
    ```
3. `/usr/bin` is not the same as `/c/Users/{user}/bin`, as `/usr/bin` is actually `C:\Program Files\Git\bin`

>Perhaps on Windows (Git Bash) starship should be installed to `/c/Users/<username>/bin` by default.

Perhaps, but I would argue that defaulting into `/usr/local/bin` is the right call, as the installation shouldn't be creating directories blindly. `C:\Users\{user}\bin` has to be created manually, as it does not exist in typical setups.

For my installation I have used the same path as `pipx`-installed packages; `~/.local/bin`. But this directory doesn't exist by default, and since the end-user can decide where to install by passing a value to `--bin-dir`, you have the choice to install (almost) wherever you'd like.

Maybe a section under `Advanced Installation` for Git Bash for Windows can be added to avoid confusion.

Finally, I have created a guide of sorts for [installing Starship on Git Bash for Windows](https://thecesrom.dev/2022/01/21/installing-starship-on-git-bash-for-windows/).

I would like to note, as a high-level thing, that we're slowly revamping our docs to be more specific to OS and shell. The README revamp a few months ago was the first step in this direction--eventually, we want to have similar per-OS and per-shell instructions in the website as well.

As of right now, `curl | sh` installation is *not* suggested as an official method by the README, and I suspect it will not be a suggested method for Windows once we update the instructions on the website.

I don't intend to drop support for git bash from the project, but I also don't think the amount of work we'd need to put in to make a single friendly script across both Windows and Linux would be worth it compared to just splitting into two install scripts, or using something like [webi](https://webinstall.dev/)
